    // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T   \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792953926713,"sessionID":"ses_e8ba26eefffePmXbMjKiaL89rP","part":{"id":"prt_174618952001Ue1AGVto4Ntp2x","messageID":"msg_17461853a001ta4whXBxDWiPJQ","sessionID":"ses_e8ba26eefffePmXbMjKiaL89rP","type":"reasoning","text":"The kernel itself runs 113ms, so most of the 8.8s total is elsewhere—host-side packing of 1e8 elements, the 977ms H2D transfer moving 5.6GB, plus D2H and cudaFree overhead. I'm trying to account for where the remaining time is actually going.\n\nLikely the vector zero-initialization and page-faulting on first touch of 5.6GB host memory accounts for several seconds not captured in the obvious timers. The real fix is avoiding the host-side AoS-to-SoA repack entirely—maybe by generating SoA data directly rather than transforming after the fact, though that would require restructuring generateOptions without breaking validation logic.\n\nI'm weighing a cleaner design: keep host generation untimed, then time only H2D transfer, kernel, and D2H. Uploading the AoS struct directly instead of repacking into SoA avoids extra host memory and packing cost, even though it means 72B/option stride reads on device—still fine since the kernel is compute-bound, not memory-bound. At 1e8 options, transfer time (~1s pageable) still dwarfs kernel time, so overall speedup versus the 9s CPU baseline lands around 9x.\n\nI'm also considering pinning the existing host vector via cudaHostRegister rather than allocating new pinned memory, which would push H2D closer to PCIe peak bandwidth, though the registration cost itself needs to be included in timing. Generating options directly on the GPU would eliminate transfer overhead entirely and be the fastest option, but since the original benchmark never timed generateOptions, doing so changes what's being measured—so I lean toward keeping generation on the host, untimed, as in the original.\n\nI'll keep the timed region focused on pricing plus transfers for honesty, switching to a raw AoS upload with a plain cudaMemcpy instead of repacking data, then D2H the results. The kernel will take a pointer to the struct array directly and read each option as a whole 72-byte struct, which may be slightly uncoalesced but should be handled fine by L2 cache. I'll test this AoS approach and possibly compare against a pinned-memory variant, and I should rewrite priceOptionsOnGpu with a simpler kernel signature taking the options array, results array, and count.\n\n","time":{"start":1792953911634,"end":1792953926648},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
